sentences.text: The name Ignotosaurus translates to 'unknown lizard,' a title earned because scientists have found only a single right ilium fossil.
This specific bone measures approximately 70 mm in length, making it impossible to determine the animal's total size with accuracy.
The specific name 'fragilis' describes the ilium's blade, which features a central portion that is only 1 mm thick.
The bone displays a saddle-shaped lateral profile and is notably longer than it is deep.
A supraacetabular crest runs laterally along the bone and assists in forming the socket where the femur attaches.
The preacetabular process angles at 90 degrees to the iliac blade and points anterolaterally, serving as a key diagnostic feature for the species.
The genus Ignotosaurus was formally described by Martínez and colleagues in 2013.
The type species designated for this genus is Ignotosaurus fragilis.
Ignotosaurus was likely a herbivore that competed for vegetation with rhynchosaurs, cynodonts, and early dinosaurs.
Ignotosaurus is classified within the family Silesauridae.
Taxonomically, it falls within the unranked group Dinosauriformes.
Researchers believe it is closely related to Silesaurus, Sacisaurus, and Eucoelophysis, although this connection remains uncertain due to the scarcity of fossil evidence.
This creature lived between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
It inhabited northwestern Argentina during the Late Triassic, sharing river basin environments with early dinosaurs like Herrerasaurus.
